task.title: Remove code cleanliness gates from independent Backlog authoring guidance
task.description:
## Outcome and operator scope
Correct independent Backlog task-only publication in both managed authoring guidance and the narrow runtime lifecycle status publisher. Parent code cleanliness/upstream equality is not a prerequisite for a task-only operation; preserving code is the requirement. Joe explicitly expanded this same PRIMECLAW-53 task: “commit your change or roll it back, whichever makes more sense. Then add these fixes to primeclaw-53. Then plan out primeclaw-53 if it isn't already planned.” This supersedes the earlier documentation-only scope and runtime-change exclusion for the specific lifecycle correction below, not for unrelated runtime work.

The original bounded Markdown correction/global delivery authority remains recorded: Joe asked for the correction in Prime Claw's global template and ADAPT's local skill. Adapt-Hand Expert owns the separate ADAPT local/symlink/gitignore/task work; ADAPT-1 is not this task. Completed PRIMECLAW-51 and PRIMECLAW-47 are not reopened. This revision records and plans the additional runtime fix; it does not authorize starting its implementation, another Episode, merge, broad activation, restart, or cleanup.

## Authoring correction
Both `src/prime-agent-plugin/skills/project-templates/design.md` and `spec-it-out.md`, in Verify and publish exactly once → Backlog, incorrectly require the parent code checkout to be clean/upstream-equal for an independent task store. Scope the index/task-path checks to the selected store and use this previously approved replacement block consistently in both templates:

### Backlog

Before mutation, record Git status in the code repository and the selected task
store. Require the selected existing task path and the selected task store's
Git index to be clean; do not apply task-store cleanliness checks to a separate
parent code repository. After creation or revision, reload the exact task
through `backlog task view --json -- TASK-ID` and verify its canonical ID,
`In Design` status, meaningful Description, native Acceptance Criteria, and
returned regular task path. Verify no path other than that exact returned task
path was newly changed in the task store and do not stage unrelated pre-existing
changes.

Preserve the selected store topology. If the selected Backlog store is a
validated ignored independent ordinary-Git clone, whether built-in or custom,
before the native task write require the independent clone to be clean and at
the directly proved `refs/heads/prime-claw/tasks` head. After the native task
write, verify only the exact intended task path changed, commit only that path
inside the clone, push `HEAD:refs/heads/prime-claw/tasks` without force, and prove
the direct remote head. There is no requirement for the parent code repository to be clean
or upstream-equal for task creation, revision, or task-store publication.
Unrelated staged, unstaged, or untracked code changes and code-branch divergence
are not blockers. Preserve the parent code HEAD, index, and worktree as found;
never commit, stash, reset, clean, or otherwise repair code changes to enable a
task-only operation. This does not relax separate implementation or Episode
admission requirements.
Only for an actual branch-local store, keep the existing flow: commit only the
returned task path in the code repository, prove the commit contains no other
path, and attempt one prompt push when a remote is available. A push failure is
transport evidence to report, not permission to undo the valid local
specification, create another task, or begin planning.

## Lifecycle correction and observed failure
In `src/prime-agent-plugin/extension-support/spec-episode.ts`, `commitConversationTaskStatus` applies parent-code cleanliness/upstream-equality checks before and after independent Backlog status publication. Episode allocation writes tracked `.prime-claw/ownership.json`. When session binding fails, automatic Blocked publication encounters that own write and rejects its own recovery with “Independent Backlog Blocked publication requires exact clean upstream-equal code HEAD”. The separate launcher/daemon mismatch caused the launch failure; the publisher's inability to report that failure is this Prime Claw defect.

For the independent Backlog path only, remove parent-code cleanliness/upstream-equality as task-status publication requirements. Use the existing native task-store preparation/publication surfaces. Before native mutation, require the exact selected independent task store clean and synchronized to its directly proved published task ref. Retain exact provider/root/task/path identity, expected source status and meaningful-plan checks where already required, exact intended task-path changes, task-store index safety, scoped task-only commit, non-force push and direct-remote proof. Preserve parent code HEAD, index and working files as found rather than requiring them clean. Unrelated staged, unstaged or untracked code, code-branch divergence and the allocation's ownership write must not prevent task-only status publication. Concurrent unrelated changes are not proof the task publisher modified code; do not introduce a whole-checkout equality gate or generic snapshot/receipt framework.

Keep code implementation/admission checks separate from task publication. Evaluate their genuine clean/published-code prerequisites before allocation's ownership write, without reapplying an already-invalidated clean-parent requirement inside failure reporting. Preserve existing safe code base/placement, owner/task/resource identity, source lifecycle, branch-local Backlog, Beads and retained-specification rules. Allocation failure must be able to publish the exact truthful Blocked status/note while preserving uncertain ownership and all allocated resources; no fresh creation, second assignment, automatic cleanup or fabricated successful admission. A dirty/unpublished/unsafe task store or failed task publication remains a real blocker and must be reported honestly.

Do not solve this by ignoring, untracking, stashing, resetting, deleting or automatically committing ownership metadata. Joe separately authorized resolving this incident's pending Git change: preserving and committing the exact uncertain record is safer than removing evidence of existing resources. That one-off bookkeeping commit is not the runtime fix or a new runtime auto-commit policy.

## Current evidence and preserved blocker
The six stale metadata baselines were repaired with supported native resets in pushed code commit `5c1358b56732869465a1402beb5fa280635122ea`; skill bytes did not change. Under Joe's new commit-or-rollback instruction, the exact pending uncertain ownership record was committed/pushed as `fe61016a5eab4a41f7d10fe3ca3996d3bb0d3fc8`, without editing its bytes, rewriting historical task evidence, or changing resources.

Retain operation `b0133363-514c-419e-affc-7fc4b1042d90`, owner Conversation `01a1363a-e0f9-7628-aee4-81b03eb1e3fb`, worktree `/Users/jlanders/worktrees/prime-claw/prime-claw-primeclaw-53-episode-b0133363`, branch `JLanders/prime-claw-primeclaw-53-episode-b0133363`, original code base `5c1358b56732869465a1402beb5fa280635122ea` and its exact Orca resources. No Episode session was bound in the recorded failed allocation. The task remains Blocked; this replan does not clear or recover the uncertain allocation.

At the recorded failure, the guarded installed launcher expected `cwd-fix-v0.9.8-r1-10-gf80340d93` / `f80340d93dc3b1c6de3459b54a82f351e136f75e`, but the sole observed daemon was PID3601/build `cwd-fix-v0.9.8-r1`. Runtime drift was corroborated by both runtime owners; its trigger was not established. These are historical observations, not a claim about the current live daemon. TASK-2 Conversation `01a18414-077b-7038-85d3-6d13ece95269` owns runtime recovery and was waiting for Joe's client-closure/coordinated-restart decision. After separately authorized runtime recovery, re-read exact owner/native/Orca/provider/Git state before deciding how to recover this same uncertain operation. No creation retry, ownership edit, new resource or guard bypass follows from planning.

## Validation, delivery and limits
Use the least-tech correction in the existing publisher/caller seams and existing tests. Add focused real disposable-Git lifecycle regression evidence, alongside the existing Markdown contract tests. Candidate plugin validation is Docker-only and includes `scripts/test-tier1.sh --probe` after source changes. Preserve unrelated files/index/task records; do not use live ADAPT or Nemo as fixtures or repair unrelated baseline failures. No new controller, persistent state/state machine, semantic classifier, task reconciliation, iterative plan machinery, approval receipt or retry protocol.

After separately accepted source publication, retain the original bounded global Markdown delivery to exactly `~/.prime/agent/skills/project-templates/design.md` (`project-skill-design`) and `spec-it-out.md` (`project-skill-spec-it-out`). Evaluate exact two-file replacement from accepted committed/validated source, with before/after hashes, safe replacement and only genuinely required managed provenance updates. Absence of a per-asset apply selector alone is not a blocker. Do not broad-apply unrelated runtime assets, build a delivery controller or restart. Report source publication, actual Markdown delivery and runtime activation separately. Installing/activating the added runtime code is outside this planning request and the two-file delivery authority.

No Prime Agent source/dependency change, launcher/daemon repair, initializer/symlink policy change, live migration, broad cleanup, unrelated task mutation or reopening completed work. Preserve the existing native independent-store topology, all unrelated customized local skills and prior activation evidence.

2. **Correct the existing lifecycle publisher, not the ownership store.** In the independent Backlog branch of `commitConversationTaskStatus` in `extension-support/spec-episode.ts`, remove the pre/post parent-code clean/upstream-equal requirements. 3. **Add focused regressions in existing suites.** Extend `tests/test_future_plan_skills.py` with small assertions for both approved Markdown blocks and their task-store/admission boundaries. Cover dirty or unpublished task history, wrong identity/source status and publication failure; preserve the existing branch-local/Beads and code-admission safeguards. 4. **Validate and report proportionately.** Run `scripts/test-tier1.sh --probe` after plugin-source changes and the existing Docker test entrypoints for the focused Markdown, spec-Episode and any directly affected task-history tests. 5. **Preserve recovery and delivery boundaries.** Before implementation can resume, obtain separately verified runtime recovery from the TASK-2 owning Conversation, then inspect current exact PRIMECLAW-53 owner/native/provider/Git/Orca state. The saved ownership evidence committed as `fe61016a5eab4a41f7d10fe3ca3996d3bb0d3fc8` remains unchanged. Report that the operator-expanded task differs from the historical taskEvidence captured at failed allocation; never forge that evidence or infer execution authority from a new plan.

6. **Accepted source and two-file Markdown delivery.** After separately authorized implementation/review/acceptance and ordinary source publication, the owning Conversation handles only the two previously authorized global Markdown destinations and asset IDs in Description. Evaluate direct exact two-file replacement from committed/validated accepted source with before/after hashes, safe replacement and only truly required provenance updates; do not treat missing per-asset CLI selection as a blocker by itself. Preserve all unrelated global/project/runtime files and processes. Do not run broad `manage-prime-agent-delivery.py apply`, add a delivery controller, install the new runtime code, or restart under this authority. task.title: Drop Beads deferral state during Backlog migration
task.description:
## Outcome
During one-way Beads→Backlog migration, import a native Beads task whose status is `deferred` as an ordinary `In Design` task. Drop active deferral state and deferral-only structured fields from the destination projection. Do not modify the retiring Beads source to achieve this.

## Product instruction and context
Joe’s instruction, relayed by NemoHermes Upgrade: “Just drop any "deferred" status and related fiedls as part of the migratino.” This supersedes the earlier unapproved proposal that the task must remain frozen or outside ready work. The selected behavior is the normal new/open task default, not a special destination lifecycle or scheduling feature.

NemoHermes Upgrade reports canonical inspection at Nemo housekeeping commit `b8c9be358df4fc5fc67d1aec74feb7c4943572e1` stops with `Beads source lifecycle preflight failed: nemo-setup-5lt status="deferred": unsupported status`. The task is titled `DEFERRED: Decide + enable web search provider`, with `defer_until=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z`. The reported native catalog defines deferred as frozen; the issue inventory is 33 issues (30 closed, one open, one blocked, one deferred), separate from the last-observed 19 memory records. These are reported consultation facts, not a new live inspection or proof of destination memory outputs.

The accepted importer currently projects fixed canonical Beads lifecycle names plus legacy open/closed and rejects deferred during source preflight. No existing runtime mapping override exists; semantic-placement prose does not change that projection. This task is the narrow destination-behavior change, not a repair of malformed source or another memory parser change.

## Required behavior
- Recognize native Beads `deferred` in inspection and destination conversion as the ordinary `In Design` projection. Use the same meaning in destination verification/replay; do not let source classification reject this selected case before projection.
- Do not create a Deferred status, active `defer_until` or other deferral-only destination fields, snooze/auto-wake behavior, special deferral annotations, or forced Draft/Blocked/archive placement. Timed, expired and indefinite source deferral do not change this destination meaning.
- Preserve ordinary title, description, notes, comments, native history and provenance. Native `bd defer --reason` appends ordinary notes; it is not a dedicated field to strip. Do not delete or rewrite ordinary text merely because it contains “deferred”, including the reported title.
- Retain the canonical raw source-capture and receipt/provenance evidence already required for lossless history. Historical deferral values may remain inside that existing raw evidence; do not restore them as active destination fields, scheduling or additional deferral annotations.
- Keep Beads unchanged and authoritative until the existing verified cutover. Never call ready/defer/undefer/status/config edits to normalize source data. Keep safe refusal for other genuinely unmapped statuses and preserve existing identity, relationship, publication, ownership, receipt/replay and guarded-retirement protections.

## Scope and authority
Use the least technology needed for this one supported projection and its focused regression coverage. Update directly affected guidance if it would otherwise contradict the behavior. No generic mapping/override framework, new controller, dependency upgrade, scheduling feature, unrelated importer cleanup, or reopening completed PRIMECLAW-44/46/49. Their accepted guarantees remain context, not unfinished work.

Authoring this task does not approve an implementation plan, implementation, merge, global activation, restart or live migration/source deletion. Candidate validation must use disposable fixtures and the repository’s Docker-only plugin workflow, including the mandatory Tier 1 probe after plugin-source changes. Do not run another live Nemo inspection to bypass the current guard or change Nemo tasks, provider or configuration. Planning and later lifecycle actions require their normal separate authority.

task.title: Allow Episode initiation during unrelated ticket edits and task-history advances
task.description:
## Outcome and authority boundary
Remove hard-coded task-native lifecycle policy from prime-claw code and put the rules and decisions in editable Markdown skills and workflows. Apply the fix to the complete task-native lifecycle for both Backlog and Beads, not just Episode initiation. This is the required code change, not an instruction-only workaround.

Code manages lifecycle stages and execution mechanics: load the applicable Markdown, inject it at the appropriate lifecycle event, invoke supported native operations, and return their factual results. The LLM follows the editable skills to apply workflow rules and make specification/planning, admission, readiness, execution, continuation, oversight, reconciliation, and terminal/finalization decisions within operator authority. Do not independently implement the same policy as TypeScript checks, hidden guards, approval locks, or another rules engine.

In particular, remove repository-wide cleanliness gates throughout initiation and supporting task resolution, preparation, status publication, and pre-session paths. Unrelated task or code edits and unrelated published task-history advances MUST NOT block Episode initiation. Other Conversations' bytes, staging, history, ownership, and resources must remain intact.

## Operator clarification
Joe explicitly rejected hard-coded workflow rules as over-engineering. Moving or renaming the checks inside other code files does not satisfy this task. Checks and reasoning about cleanliness, selected-ticket commit/publication prerequisites, implementation readiness, task lifecycle eligibility, code-base suitability, and compatibility of changing task/history observations belong to LLMs following editable skills/workflows, not a second code-level admission policy. Code may read lifecycle facts to route the relevant Markdown stage; it must not use routing as a disguised policy gate. Native failures and resource-operation results must still be reported truthfully.

The confirmed Beads defect includes prime-claw's whole-code-repository cleanliness checks in proveBeadsAdmissionCodeHead and reservePublishedBeadsTaskEpisodeOwnership. This does not claim Beads has the exact independent-Backlog race recorded below. Each Episode obtains task context through its provider's workspace/history. Backlog uses its exact-task Git history; Beads uses native task-history commit/publication rather than a fabricated Markdown/Git task path. task.implementationPlan:
## Implementation approach
Make this a removal-and-relocation refactor, not a new policy framework. Editable Markdown and the invoking LLM own the complete Backlog and Beads task-native lifecycle. Code loads the relevant stage, supplies current native facts, performs explicitly requested supported operations, and reports their results. Keep operator authority unchanged. Existing tests and historical guard names do not create requirements. Deliver coherent slices of this one task, changing code, guidance and tests together; do not introduce another lifecycle protocol.

### 1. Map the current paths, then move policy before removing its duplicate
Trace task-native specification/planning, initiation, execution, handoff/continuation, oversight/review, block/resume, and terminal/finalization through `extensions/reviewed-plan.ts`, `extension-support/prep-chain.ts`, `workflow-chain.ts`, `spec-episode.ts`, `task-history-workspace.ts`, `task-providers.ts`, `task-episode-ownership.ts`, `task-episode-cleanup.ts`, and the existing oversight/handoff injection paths. Use the existing asset inventory and story traceability to avoid missing a stage; do not add a policy registry or second requirements document.

Put the actual rules in the existing entry skills, project skills, and canonical workflows. Move policy prose from tool descriptions/snippets/parameter descriptions/`promptGuidelines` and generated prompt suffixes into Markdown too; leave concise mechanical API descriptions and factual bindings. Reuse current workflow/guide loaders. Wire each affected operation to the right current guidance and native observations, including initial execute and later review/cleanup; no hard-coded fallback policy, new rules engine, or approval receipt.

### 2. Remove shared and Backlog code-policy gates end to end
Change the production task-resolution, preparation, publication, reservation, allocation, continuation and terminal paths, not only the two initially reported dirty checks. Make selected-task reads observational: `resolveSynchronizedProviderTask` must not implicitly bootstrap/synchronize/relocate another workspace, and Backlog configuration/status capability checks must not hide an otherwise readable native task. Separate factual reads from explicitly requested preparation. In `task-history-workspace.ts` and its callers, remove whole-primary/nested-clone cleanliness, whole-index changed-path counts, stale whole-branch equality and paired stable-head requirements as workflow prerequisites. An Episode can obtain the selected committed/published task through its existing native history workspace without first synchronizing another Conversation’s dirty primary checkout. Keep supported independent and grandfathered branch-local layouts; do not introduce another task authority/store. Remove the existing multi-round stable-read/push-retry/other-task-classifier/automatic-merge reconciliation in `publishTaskHistoryMutation` and its helpers, rather than extending it. Reuse direct native task edit and exact-path Git commit/non-force push; report before/after facts and actual conflicts for the LLM to interpret.

In `spec-episode.ts`, `prep-chain.ts`, tool entry callbacks and ownership helpers, remove duplicate lifecycle-status/design/readiness, selected-ticket-publication and primary-main/clean-upstream/code-base suitability decisions. Cover ordinary handoff and terminal paths as well as initial create. Return current task/code/history/resource facts and actual native failures for Markdown-led decisions; do not relocate predicates under transport, safety, integrity, reservation or cleanup labels. Retain only proportional native I/O/transport and exact requested resource-operation mechanics, including addressing the correct existing owner entry, session, worktree and ref without overwriting foreign resources. Do not add new lock/approval state.

### 3. Apply the same extraction to every Beads path
Remove the Beads-specific eligibility, clean-whole-working-set, exact local/remote/paired-revision, frozen task-content, status/design and code-head gates in provider reads/transport, creation/reservation, continuation/evidence advancement and terminal cleanup. Relevant seams include `checkBeadsCapabilities`, `prepareSelectedBeadsWorkspaceTransport`, `exactBeadsAdmissionTask`, `proveBeadsAdmissionCodeHead`, `reservePublishedBeadsTaskEpisodeOwnership`, `advancePublishedBeadsTaskEpisodeEvidence`, `mutateAndPublishBeadsTaskStatus` and terminal-task readers. Do not leave Beads behind after fixing Backlog.

Obtain only the native observations needed for the current stage through existing interfaces. Do not build a universal observation layer, cached snapshot schema, or repeated whole-store publication-proof pipeline. When reading a task, preserve its complete native long view, status and field absence, including unmapped/closed statuses; do not hide them behind a canonical-status refusal or fabricate a Backlog path/normalized mirror. Ensure fresh native context reaches initial execute and subsequent stage guidance without creating another store or assignment. Native CLI conditions may be executed when explicitly requested by the LLM; they are not hidden plugin transition rules.

### 4. Make lifecycle decisions and ticket durability explicit in Markdown
Move status-transition orchestration and failure disposition out of code. In particular, code must not choose automatic rollback to In Planning versus Blocked from an exception, decide semantic compatibility of observations, or decide terminal eligibility before exposing current facts. Existing owner guidance directs native provider/Git commands for status, blockers/resume, Ready/Request Changes, merge/abandonment and cleanup. Preserve Conversation status ownership, Episode content ownership and read-only Expert review. Explicit operator merge/abandonment authority and automatic exact cleanup after its published terminal outcome remain the same; moving the rules grants no new authority.

Update shipped `implement-task` and both canonical implementation workflows so the invoking Agent commits and, when a remote exists, publishes the selected coherent ticket before the Episode needs it. Use exact-task ordinary Git history for Backlog and native history for Beads. This remains an Agent duty, not a native approval-revision or cleanliness check. On real native conflicts or uncertain consequential results, preserve facts and use current evidence/LLM judgment; no automatic reconcile/retry/fresh allocation.

Complete the secondary durability audit across every Markdown asset in `asset-inventory.json`, the repo’s managed `.agents/skills/` and `.prime-claw/workflows/` copies, additional `.agents/skills/backlog`/AGENTS guidance, and role/continuation fragments. Cover creation, specification, planning, content/plan/evidence edits, accepted review findings, blockers/status and terminal updates. Each coherent authorized ticket edit is committed ASAP and published promptly, not saved for handoff/compaction/session end. Remove conflicting whole-store/index/code cleanliness instructions and obsolete claims that a separate host gate still enforces policy. Preserve unrelated bytes/staging/history/fields and customize exact paths rather than blanket-copying/resetting project assets. Fix independent-history Expert guidance so the task is read from native task history, not assumed to be in the code candidate commit.

### 5. Support only the recorded same-operation recovery
Add the bounded owner procedure to existing implementation/blocked/oversight guidance for PRIMECLAW-45’s allocated-worktree/pre-session shape. Inspect current exact operation/resource and actual session/assignment-delivery facts first. Missing recorded session identity alone does not establish that execution never started. Continue only the owning Conversation’s same operation, task, code base, selected host, branch and worktree; reuse an existing session/assignment where present and report genuine ambiguity instead of replaying it.

Reuse the existing allocator’s post-worktree task-preparation, launch/session and identity-binding operations. Expose only the missing existing-operation continuation through the current task lifecycle surface, explicitly bound to the recorded operation identity; it must not re-enter reservation/worktree allocation or count as fresh admission. Keep the decision/procedure in Markdown and only the requested action/identity update in code. Do not add a general recovery API/state machine, hand-edit ownership or duplicate resources/assignments. Reproduce this with disposable fixtures. Do not mutate the live PRIMECLAW-45 resources, implement its dependency upgrade, or expand into the separate general allocation-recovery/direct-work/stacked-base features.

### 6. Replace obsolete policy tests with focused behavior coverage
Update tests alongside each coherent source/guidance slice. Exercise the production/default resolver and tool paths: the existing Backlog admission integration injects plain `resolveBacklogTask` and finishes its history advance before preparation, so it misses the recorded failure. Add representative dirty staged/unstaged/untracked unrelated primary task/code work and published descendants after In Progress, during pre-session preparation, after successful publication, and in handoff/blocker/terminal paths. Check preserved bytes, index entries, native fields/history and other owners/resources, not a globally clean result.

For both providers, prove edited project guidance is loaded at applicable stages and current raw facts reach the LLM without duplicate policy refusals. Cover truthful native command/transport failure, partial allocation/failure reporting and same-operation continuation without duplicate assignment. For Beads, include raw status/field absence and unrelated native-history descendants. For terminal operations, test exact requested resource targeting and preservation of foreign/shared resources; eligibility decisions belong in Markdown, not a new fake semantic classifier. Preserve retained version-1 behavior through regression coverage without redesigning it.

Use the existing Node suites and Python container bridges: `task_history_workspace`, `task_providers`, Backlog/Beads admission, ownership, `reviewed_plan`, `spec_episode`, and `episode_close`. Update static Markdown/metadata assertions that pin the obsolete host guards instead of preserving them; retain useful inventory/discovery/customization checks. Do not add an exhaustive matrix, new test framework or prose-only substitute for runtime tests.

### 7. Validate, align docs and publish the candidate
After every plugin-source change run the required Docker-only tier 1. Use `scripts/test-tier1.sh --probe` plus focused bridges via `python3 -m pytest tests/test_task_history_workspace.py tests/test_task_providers.py tests/test_reviewed_plan_extension.py -q -m container` and relevant existing stage/asset tests. Run host-safe tier-0 checks where relevant. All candidate plugin execution/probes stay isolated; no host/user-global candidate apply/check or live sandbox/provider calls.

Align task-native portions of `docs/backlog.md`, `prep-chain.md`, `handoff-chain.md`, `conversation-driven-episode-oversight.md`, relevant stories/traceability and `future-specification-bundles.md` with the new policy/mechanics boundary. Keep REQUIREMENTS G2/P6/P11 consistent without importing unrelated proposed features, and leave historical evidence historical. Follow inventory/delivery rules if assets move; preserve customized-project update semantics and foreign active snapshots. Do not activate global assets.

Commit/publish coherent code and native task updates promptly. Record the actual commands/results and limits on this task, with remaining accepted in-scope work in its living plan. Deliver a reviewable candidate only: no user-global activation/restart, live recovery, destructive cleanup, retained-folder redesign, dependency patch, merge or abandonment is included. This planning request does not authorize implementation.
